title: DR1's "View details" opens the address's own record page in the address book; the frontend's expands the same three lines that are already in the row.

finding.frontend: The last cell of every picker row is a `<details>` disclosure whose summary reads "View details", with a visually hidden " for <name>", and which expands in place to a list of the record's lines (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:26-41). Most of what it shows is already in the row — the name, the address lines and the country the Name, Address and Country columns carry — and it adds two things they do not, the telephone number and the email address (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/view-model/address-lines.js). fe-address-picker-place-of-origin renders the disclosure triangle in every row and Astra Rosales expands to seven lines against the three in the row. There is still no record history and no way to see which other notifications use the record, and the trader never leaves the picker.
finding.prototype: The same cell in DR1 is a link, not a disclosure: "View details" goes to the address book's record page for that address, carrying a return path back to the picker (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:152, href built at app/routes.js:3562). The trader leaves the picker, reads the whole record and comes back to the same role with their place kept.
finding.difference: Make "View details" a link to the address record rather than an in-page expander, so the trader reads the whole record on its page and comes back to the same role with their place kept, and drop the address lines the disclosure repeats from the row. Reproducing DR1 exactly means linking to the address book's record page in the INS front-door, because that is where the record pages live and this service reads the book and never writes it (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19) — a cross-app link with a return path, the same dependency as adding an address from the picker, and the two should be settled together. Nothing stops a read-only record page being built here instead: the address-book service already fetches one record by id, so that route is frontend-work and needs no API change. Which of the two is right is the open question, and it is the same question the add-address finding turns on.
finding.falsifiedBy: An address record page existing in trade-imports-animals-frontend, or DR1's "View details" turning out to expand in place rather than navigate.
finding.correction: Claim corrected, finding stands on its other half. It said the disclosure expands to the same lines the row already shows and so tells the trader nothing new, and that it holds no phone number and no email. Both are wrong. The rendered picker expands Astra Rosales to seven lines — name, street, town, postcode, country, `01632 960000` and `astra-rosales@example.com` — against the three cells the row shows, and the view model that builds them appends the telephone number and the email address after the country on purpose. The frontend slot is rewritten to say so, and the difference slot no longer claims the picker renders the same lines twice. The old falsifier was self-firing, because "the frontend disclosure showing any field the row does not already show" is exactly what the disclosure does; it is replaced with the two observations that would actually settle the finding. What survives is the difference that matters and it is observable on both sides: DR1's cell is a link that navigates to the record page carrying a return path, built at app/routes.js:3562 and rendered as an href in the captured page, where the frontend's is an in-page expander. Also worth saying about the band: the needs-backend argument is that this service cannot grow a record page on its own, and that is not quite true — `party(orgId, id)` already returns one record, so the band rests on the choice to send the trader to the INS record page rather than on a missing read path.

relatedTo.why: both are journeys out of the picker into the address book and share one decision about which service owns address records
